paragraphs: Rabbi Yasa, son of Rabbi Yasa’s daughter.
Mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 6:1, where he reports in the name of Rabbi Yirmeya. Hyman tentatively proposes reading Rabbi Yose ben Yose. See his entry,

notes.text: The heading’s ברכיה conflicts with the earlier reading ברתיה, and the attachment of its final דר׳ יסא remains unclear. Hyman tentatively suggests Rabbi Yose ben Yose.

The supplied ברכיה and earlier ברתיה reading, and the final דר׳ יסא attachment, remain unresolved. The personal titles are kept as R' without a new expanded-title witness, and no student/son/daughter attachment is invented. The historical כה: locator is retained alongside25b, without claiming a modern edition mapping. Hyman’s אפשר remains tentative and the terminal comma remains. Earlier reported Nazir6:1/search nonmatches are not new whole-chapter inspection or proof of absence across spellings.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 742) reads בר ברתיה דר׳ יסא, where the supplied Hebrew has בר ברכיה דר׳ יסא. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud text and translation call him Rabbi Yasa, son of Rabbi Yasa’s daughter, and give Rabbi Yirmeya as his source. Hyman cites כה: (25b). The corresponding passage falls on 26a in the consulted edition’s Vilna pagination. His suggestion of Rabbi Yose ben Yose remains tentative.
